title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is a political impersonation carried out with a generative video tool. The system was used to produce footage of a candidate saying things she did not say, and the output was published to a social media account as if it were real speech. The failure sits at the point of publication rather than at the point of generation: nothing in the described workflow placed a check between producing the clip and posting it to voters.

Catching this would not have required a technical fix. The statements attributed to Cooke were never made, so the falsehood was verifiable against the public record by anyone who cared to check before posting. The only safeguard that would have stopped it is a human decision not to publish synthetic speech as authentic, or to label it clearly as synthetic.

What is not established is whether the videos were intended to deceive, whether any legal claim will follow, and whether the cease-and-desist letter has any force. A letter is an allegation, not a finding, and the campaign's response is a statement, not a defence.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over his use of AI deepfake videos. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. Van Orden posted videos to X showing an AI-generated Cooke saying things she never said, including a clip from Aug. 4. The letter, dated Sept. 30, says Cooke never made those statements and accuses Van Orden of trying to fool voters.

Cooke's attorneys say they are monitoring Van Orden's social media and weighing all legal options if he keeps misusing AI to defame her. Van Orden's campaign dismissed the letter as a tantrum. He responded on social media with another AI video featuring a duck saying "Cease and desist!" Cooke ran for the seat in 2022 and 2024, losing to Van Orden by about 3 percentage points last time.
